# ISATVON

> ISATVON is an open, plain-text prompting framework that structures both the prompt
> and the AI response across seven sections: Instructions, Source, Automation,
> Tech stack, Variables, Outcome, Notification. It exists to make AI output
> auditable — what the model was told, what it used, how it verified itself, what
> it assumed, and what it could not do. Apache 2.0, maintained by DigiBull AI.

ISATVON is a convention, not software. It is plain text, so it works unchanged in
ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Copilot and Grok. Its distinguishing feature
against lighter frameworks such as COSTAR is that it also specifies the shape of the
answer, and requires the model to self-verify and to declare its assumptions.

## The seven sections

- **I — Instructions**: role, objective and hard rules ("never invent figures").
- **S — Source**: what context to use, and an explicit "do not assume" boundary.
- **A — Automation**: the step order, ending in a self-verification check before answering.
- **T — Tech stack**: capabilities allowed and forbidden — web search, code execution, citations.
- **V — Variables**: measurable constraints (length, tone, audience) each with a declared fallback.
- **O — Outcome**: the deliverable, plus the requirement that the reply itself is returned in ISATVON structure.
- **N — Notification**: mandatory report of assumptions, confidence level and anything omitted.

## Pages

- [ISATVON framework overview](https://www.isatvon.ai/): what the framework is, why unstructured prompts drift, the seven sections, use cases and limits.
- [How ISATVON works](https://www.isatvon.ai/how-it-works): raw request to reviewable response, and how to read an ISATVON-structured answer.
- [Prompt converter and template library](https://www.isatvon.ai/prompting): convert a raw prompt into ISATVON structure, plus before/after examples for seven AI platforms.
- [ISATVON vs COSTAR](https://www.isatvon.ai/isatvon-vs-costar): section-by-section mapping, what ISATVON adds, and when the lighter framework is the better choice.

## Machine-readable

- [Skill registry](https://github.com/solutionsDigibull/ISATVON-prompting/blob/main/skill-registry.json): name, version, trigger phrases and file inventory, generated from SKILL.md.
- [Example index](https://github.com/solutionsDigibull/ISATVON-prompting/blob/main/examples/index.json): every worked example with platform, difficulty, category and tags.
- [Templates and examples as JSON](https://www.isatvon.ai/api/templates): both templates and all examples, generated from the repository markdown.
- [Prompt conversion API](https://www.isatvon.ai/openapi.yaml): OpenAPI description of POST /api/convert and GET /api/templates.

## When not to use ISATVON

Not for one-line factual lookups, casual conversation, or strict machine-execution
contracts — deterministic agent loops with schemas, retries and guaranteed tool calls
need a machine-readable specification and validator, not a prompting convention.
ISATVON also cannot rescue analysis built on incomplete or unreliable sources, and it
does not replace expert review for legal, medical, financial or security decisions.
